titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Solomon Returns to Jerusalem and Is Consoled (ch. 61)
part: ch. 61 — Solomon Returns to Jerusalem and Is Consoled
about: Solomon re-enters Jerusalem and weeps with the elders and Zadok over the Ark's departure. His counsellors console him: Zion stays or goes by God's will and her own, as the Ark's history already showed among the Philistines (Dagon, the plague, the Philistine gold, the two animals and the cart), under Samuel, Saul and David. They end by reminding him that the wisdom God gave him is his own and that fools' words cannot harm it.

sentences.t: ፷፩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ግብአተ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ።
sentences.l: 61. Concerning return-of Solomon (to) Jerusalem
sentences.i: Chapter 61: Concerning Solomon's Return to Jerusalem
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ 'concerning' takes the construct ግብአተ 'return-of' (verbal noun of ገብአ 'return, come back', as in the published parts), which governs the name ሰሎሞን; ኢየሩሳሌም follows as the place entered (no preposition). ፷፩ is the printed Ethiopic numeral, 60 + 1.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ አተወ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወበከየ ፡ በህየኒ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አእሩገ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ብካየ ፡ ዐቢየ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-after-this he-entered city-of Jerusalem, and-he-wept in-there-also with elders-of Jerusalem weeping great in-midst house-of God;
sentences.i: Then he entered the city of Jerusalem and wept there too, together with the elders of Jerusalem, weeping greatly within the house of God.
sentences.n: ወእምዝ 'and-after-this'. አተወ 'he entered' (G perfect) with the place as direct object, ሀገረ is construct 'city-of'. በህየኒ = በ-ህየ 'in there' + enclitic -ኒ 'also'. አእሩገ is construct plural 'elders-of' (አእሩግ, plural of አረጋዊ 'old man, elder'). ብካየ ዐቢየ 'great weeping' is a cognate accusative (the noun of the verb በከየ, as in the published ብካየ መሪረ). ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር is the Temple Solomon built. Solomon comes back from the pursuit of the Ethiopians (chs. 57–58) to a Jerusalem without the Ark.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅረዝ ፡ ተኣኀዙ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሰዶቅ ፡ ካህን ፡ በክሳውዲሆሙ ፡ ወበከዩ ፡ መሪረ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ምንባሪሃ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ወአርመሙ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ጒንዱይ ፡ ሰዐት ።
sentences.l: And-after-this they-took-hold(reciprocal) king with Zadok priest by-their-necks(?), and-they-wept bitterly in-midst her-seat of-Zion, and-they-fell-silent after a-lingering(?) hour.
sentences.i: After that the king and Zadok the priest clasped one another by the neck and wept bitterly in the place where Zion had sat; and after a long while (?) they fell silent.
sentences.n: ተኣኀዙ is 3mp of ተኣኀዘ, the reflexive/reciprocal stem 'take hold of one another', so the plural verb covers 'king ... with Zadok'. ክሳውዲሆሙ 'their necks' is my reading of an irregular plural of ክሳድ 'neck' (?). መሪረ 'bitterly' is an adverbial accusative. ምንባሪሃ ለጽዮን 'her seat, of Zion' (anticipatory pronoun + ለ, the usual way to mark a genitive after a suffixed noun): the Ark's resting-place in the Temple. ወአርመሙ 'they fell silent' (አርመመ). ጒንዱይ ሰዐት 'a lingering hour' = 'a long while' (?): ጒንዱይ is glossed as the noun 'lingering, delay' in the published entry (here qualifying ሰዐት); since እምድኅረ is 'after', the silence follows the long weeping. Zadok the priest is the high priest of Solomon's day.

sentences.t: ወተንሥኡ ፡ መላህቅት ፡ ወተናገርዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብሉ ፡ ኢትሕዝን ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ በእንተዝ ፡ ነገር ፡ እስመ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ አእመርነ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኢትነብር ፡ ጽዮን ፡ እምቀዳሚ ፡ እስከ ፡ ደኃሪ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይከውን ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ በፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-arose the-elders(?) and-spoke-to-him to-the-king saying: Do-not-grieve, our-lord, over-this matter, for we know that-except where wished God not-stays Zion from-first to last, and-there-is-not what happens except by-will-of God;
sentences.i: Then the elders rose and spoke to the king, saying, 'Do not grieve, our lord, over this matter. We know that Zion stays nowhere except where God wishes, from first to last, and nothing happens except by God's will;
sentences.n: መላህቅት is a plural noun I take as 'elders, leading men' (?), related to ልሕቀ 'grow great'; the sense is a council of senior men consoling the king. ወተናገርዎ ለንጉሥ: verb + -ዎ 'him', then ለ- again marks the person addressed. እንዘ ይብሉ 'while saying' introduces direct speech. ኢትሕዝን 2ms jussive 'do not grieve'. በእንተዝ = በእንተ + ዝ 'concerning this'. ዘእንበለ ኀበ ፈቀደ 'except to-where he wished'. ኢትነብር ጽዮን: Zion (the Ark) is feminine; ነብረ 'sit, dwell'. ወአልቦ ዘይከውን 'there is none/nothing that happens'. The theology of the Ark's free movement is the core of this chapter.

sentences.t: ወዘበእንተ ፡ ጽዮንሂ ፡ ቀዲሙ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ኤሊ ፡ ካህን ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ይስአሉ ፡ አበዊነ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ፄወውዋ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ትዕይንት ፡ ሶበ ፡ ተሀየዮሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ በውስተ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ ወወድቁ ፡ ካህናቲሃ ፡ አፍኒ ፡ ወፊናሐስ ፡ በአፈ ፡ ኀጺን ፡ ወነሥእዋ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ለታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወአእተውዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገሮሙ ፡ ወወደይዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ አምላኮሙ ፡ ዳጎን ፤
sentences.l: And-concerning-Zion-also, earlier, in-days-of Eli priest, before they-asked our-fathers a-king, led-her-captive the-Philistines in-midst the-camp, when turned-from(?)-them God Israel in-midst battle, and-fell her-priests Hophni and-Phinehas by-mouth-of iron, and-took-her the-Philistines, Ark-of his-law of-God, and-brought-her into their-land and-put-her in-midst house-of their-god Dagon;
sentences.i: And as for Zion too, long ago, in the days of Eli the priest, before our fathers asked for a king, the Philistines carried her off in the midst of the camp, when God turned away from Israel (?) in the battle: her priests Hophni and Phinehas fell by the edge of the sword, and the Philistines took the Ark of God's law, brought it into their own land, and set it in the house of their god Dagon;
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 4–5: Eli, his sons Hophni and Phinehas, the Philistines (ኢሎፍሊ, from the Septuagint's Greek allophyloi 'foreigners') and Dagon. ዘበእንተ ጽዮንሂ 'what concerns Zion also' (-ሂ enclitic). ዘእንበለ ይስአሉ 'before they asked' (ዘእንበለ + subjunctive 'before'), ንጉሠ 'a king' accusative (1 Samuel 8). ፄወውዋ 'they carried her off captive' (ፄወወ 'take captive') + -ዋ 'her'. ትዕይንት 'camp, battle-array'. ተሀየዮሙ: root and sense uncertain (?); I keep the house reading 'turned away from' (chs. 30, 60), with ለእስራኤል naming Israel. በአፈ ኀጺን 'by the mouth of iron' = by the sword (Hebrew idiom). ለታቦተ: ለ- marks the object, ታቦተ is construct 'Ark-of'; ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'his law, God's' is a resumptive genitive. Dagon is the Philistine god.

sentences.t: ወተሰብረ ፡ ወተሀጒለ ፡ ዳጎን ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ጸበል ፡ ወምድሮሙ ፡ ኮነት ፡ በድወ ፡ በአና ፡ ጹት ፡ ወበልዐ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ፍሬ ፡ ምድሮሙ ፡ ወነፍስቶሙኒ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ጸልዐ ፡ ወሕበጠ ፤
sentences.l: And-was-broken and-was-destroyed Dagon, and-became like dust(?), and-their-land became desert by-mice(?) 'ጹት', and-it-devoured all fruit-of their-land, and-their-persons-also became an-ulcer(?) and-swelling(?);
sentences.i: Dagon was broken and destroyed and became like dust (?); their land turned to desert through the mice (?), which ate all the produce of their land; and their own bodies too became ulcerous and swollen (?);
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 5–6 (Dagon fallen, the plague of tumours, the mice). ተሰብረ ወተሀጒለ 'was broken and was destroyed' are reflexive/passive (ተ-) forms. ጸበል: I read 'dust, ashes' (?). በድወ 'desert' (በድው), predicate of ኮነት. The printed words በአና ፡ ጹት are broken: ጹት stands alone. The same word appears whole at unit 13 as አናጹት, so I read 'by mice' (?), with 'አና ጹት' kept exactly as printed. ወበልዐ 'and it devoured' is masculine singular, subject apparently the mice (collective). ጸልዐ and ሕበጠ read as accusative nouns (ጸልዕ 'ulcer', ሕበጥ 'swelling', as in units 6 and 13; the accusative ends in -ä), both predicates of ኮነ: 'became an ulcer and a swelling' (?).

sentences.t: ወአስተጋብኡ ፡ ማርያኒሆሙ ፡ ወመሰግላኒሆሙ ፡ ወረአይተ ፡ ከዋክብቲሆሙ ፡ ወተስእልዎሙ ፡ ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ እፎ ፡ ንድኅን ፡ እምዝጸልዕ ፡ ወምንዳቤ ፡ ዘረከበነ ፡ ለነ ፡ ወለሀገርነ ፤
sentences.l: And-gathered their-priests(?) and-their-diviners and-observers-of their-stars and-asked them and-said-to-them: How may-we-be-saved from-this-ulcer and-affliction that-befell us, us and-our-land?
sentences.i: They gathered their priests (?), their diviners and their star-readers and asked them, 'How can we be saved from this ulcer and affliction that has come upon us and our land?'
sentences.n: ማርያኒሆሙ: ማርያን is a title I take as 'priests' of the pagan cult (?), as in 1 Samuel 6:2 where the Philistines call priests and diviners; the word is not clear to me and the later unit 13 repeats it. መሰግላኒሆሙ 'their diviners' (an agent noun in መ-, from ሰገል 'divination, sorcery' (?), as in the published ወሰገል; I know no verb ሰገለ). ረአይተ ከዋክብቲሆሙ 'seers-of their stars' (construct 'observers-of'). ተስእልዎሙ 'they questioned them'. እፎ ንድኅን 'how may we be saved' (1cp subjunctive). ዝጸልዕ = ዝ + ጸልዕ 'this ulcer'. ዘረከበነ ለነ 'that found us, us' with ለ- repeating the object for emphasis.

sentences.t: ኀለዩ ፡ እሙንቱ ፡ መሰግላን ፡ ተግሒሦሙ ፡ እንተ ፡ ባሕቲቶሙ ፡ ወአምጽኡ ፡ ሰገላቲሆሙ ፡ ወኀለዩ ፡ ወሐሰቡ ፡ ወመከሩ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ እፎ ፡ ይድኅኑ ፡ እምንዳቤ ፡ ሀገሮሙ ፡ ወነፍስቶሙ ፤
sentences.l: They-considered those diviners, having-withdrawn(?), by-themselves (lit. which-is their-aloneness), and-brought their-divinations(?), and-considered and-reckoned and-took-counsel how they-might-be-saved from-affliction-of their-land and-their-persons;
sentences.i: The diviners considered the matter, withdrawing by themselves; they brought out their divinations (?), and considered, reckoned and took counsel on how they might be saved from the affliction of their land and their own persons;
sentences.n: ኀለዩ 'they considered'. ተግሒሦሙ: I take this as a gerund 'having withdrawn, they' (ተግሕሠ 'turn aside', glossed so in earlier parts; stem uncertain (?)). እንተ ባሕቲቶሙ 'which is their aloneness' = 'by themselves'. ሰገላቲሆሙ 'their divinations' (plural of ሰገል 'divination, sorcery' (?); 'instruments' or 'results' is a guess). ሐሰቡ 'they reckoned'. ዘከመ እፎ 'how, in what way'. ይድኅኑ 3mp subjunctive 'they be saved'. ነፍስቶሙ 'their selves/persons' (plural of ነፍስ), the Geʿez way to say 'themselves'.

sentences.t: ወረከቡ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ከመ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ዘረከቦሙ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ መቅሠፍት ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ወለሀገሮሙ ።
sentences.l: And-they-found this: that on-account-of Zion that-befell-them this scourge, them and-their-land.
sentences.i: They concluded that this scourge had come upon them and their land because of Zion.
sentences.n: ወረከቡ ዘንተ 'they found this' (ረከበ), followed by a ከመ clause 'that'. ዘረከቦሙ 'which befell them' is the relative ዘ used to carry the clause; መቅሠፍት 'scourge, plague' (from ቀሠፈ 'strike, scourge'); ሎሙ ወለሀገሮሙ repeats 'them and their land' with ለ-.

sentences.t: ወሖሩ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነገሥቶሙ ፡ ወመኳንንቲሆሙ ፡ ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘረከበክሙ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-they-went to their-kings and-their-governors and-said-to-them: All-this that-befell-you is on-account-of Zion, the-heavenly, Ark-of his-law of-God;
sentences.i: They went to their kings and governors and said, 'All that has come upon you is because of Zion, the heavenly one, the Ark of God's law.
sentences.n: መኳንንት 'governors, nobles'. ሰማያዊት 'heavenly' (feminine, agreeing with ጽዮን). ጽዮን here means the Ark, and 'heavenly' is the Kebra Nagast's standing epithet for it (the Ark as the earthly copy of a heavenly Zion). ታቦተ is in apposition, accusative. ዝንቱ ኵሉ 'this whole/all this'.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ አእምሩ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ታገብእዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገራ ፡ ወብሔራ ፡ ወቤታ ፤
sentences.l: And-now know how you-may-return-her into her-city and-her-land and-her-house;
sentences.i: Now consider how you may send her back to her city, her land and her house.
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ 'and now'. አእምሩ imperative 'know, consider'. ታገብእዋ 2mp subjunctive of the causative አግብአ 'make return, bring back' + -ዋ 'her'. Three nouns each with 'her': ሀገራ ብሔራ ቤታ.

sentences.t: ወአኮ ፡ ዕራቃ ፡ ዘንፌንዋ ፡ አላ ፡ ሀብዋ ፡ ሞጻ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትስረይ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ኀጢአተክሙ ፡ ወትሰስል ፡ ምንዳቤክሙ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ገብአት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገራ ፡ ወሶበሰ ፡ ኢፈነውክምዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገራ ፡ ኢኮነ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ አንብሮታ ፡ ኀቤክሙ ፡ አላ ፡ ትትቀሠፉ ፡ ኵልክሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ተኀል ፡ ቁ ።
sentences.l: And-not empty-handed(?) that-we-send her, but give-her fringe(?) that be-forgiven this your-sin and-be-lightened your-affliction when returned Zion into her-city; and-if-not you-send-her into her-city, not-good her-staying with-you, but you-will-be-scourged all-of-you until you-are-finished(?) ተኀል ቁ.
sentences.i: We are not to send her away empty-handed (?); give her a fringe-offering (?), so that this sin of yours may be forgiven and your affliction lightened once Zion has returned to her city. If you do not send her back to her city, her staying with you will not be good, but all of you will be scourged until you are finished.'
sentences.n: ዕራቃ 'naked, bare', adverbial: 'empty-handed' (?). ዘንፌንዋ is 1cp ('that we send her'): the priests include themselves, 'we are not to send her away empty-handed', then turn to the kings with the imperative ሀብዋ. ሞጻ keeps its house reading 'fringe (?)' (chs. 51–52, 55–56, where the Philistines' gold is tied to Zion's fringe), so ሀብዋ ሞጻ is 'give her fringe(-gold)', the guilt-offering of 1 Samuel 6:3–4 (?). ትስረይ 'be forgiven' (ሰረየ), ትሰስል 'be eased' (ሰሰለ, 'loosened, lightened'). ሶበ ... ወሶበሰ 'when ... but if'. ኢኮነ ሠናየ 'it would not be good'. The final tokens ተኀል ፡ ቁ are broken in the source: it is plainly ተኀልቁ 'you are finished/perish' (ኀልቀ), printed as two words, kept as printed.

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ ነገሥቶሙ ፡ ወመኳንንቲሆሙ ፡ ለማርያኒሆሙ ፡ ምንተኬ ፡ ዘትብሉ ፡ ዘንሁባ ፡ ሞጻ ፡ ወከመ ፡ እፎ ፡ ንፌንዋ ፡ ጠዪቀክሙ ፡ ንግሩነ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ንሬሲ ።
sentences.l: And-said-to-them their-kings and-their-governors to-their-priests(?): What then is-that-which you-say, that-we-give-her fringe(?), and how may-we-send her? Exactly, you, tell-us what we-should-do.
sentences.i: Their kings and governors said to their priests (?), 'What exactly are you telling us to give her as a fringe-offering (?), and how are we to send her away? Tell us precisely what we should do.'
sentences.n: ምንተኬ 'what, then?' (-ኬ enclitic). ዘትብሉ 'which you (pl.) say'. ዘንሁባ 1cp subjunctive of ወሀበ 'give', with ዘ 'that which'. ጠዪቀክሙ 'carefully, precisely, you' (ጠየቀ 'be exact'); I take it as an adverbial participle (?). ንሬሲ 1cp subjunctive of ረሰየ 'make, do'. 1 Samuel 6:2 has the Philistines put the same question to their priests and diviners.

sentences.t: ወመከሩ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ማርያነ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ ለነገሥቶሙ ፡ ወለመኳንንቲሆሙ ፡ ግበሩ ፡ ላቲ ፡ በርእሰ ፡ አብያቲክሙ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ሞጻ ፡ ፰ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ አናጹት ፡ በከመ ፡ አጥፍኡ ፡ ሀገርክሙ ፡ ወአምሳለ ፡ ነፍስተ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ፰ ፡ በከመ ፡ ሐመምክሙ ፡ ነፍስተክሙ ፡ በጸልዕ ፡ ወሕበጥ ፡ እንተ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ቊልፈትክሙ ።
sentences.l: And-they-took-counsel again the-priests(?) of-the-Philistines and-said to-their-kings and-to-their-governors: Make for-her, at head-of your-houses(?), gold, fringe(?): 8 likenesses-of mice, as they-destroyed your-land, and 8 likenesses-of a-person-of a-man, as you-were-sick your-persons with-ulcer and-swelling which is at your-backside(?).
sentences.i: The priests (?) of the Philistines took counsel again and said to their kings and governors, 'Make for her, for the heads of your households (?), a fringe-offering (?) of gold: eight images of mice, as they ruined your land, and eight images of a man's body, as you were sick in your bodies with ulcer and swelling in your hindquarters (?).'
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 6:4–5 (golden tumours and golden mice). The text prints ፰ 'eight' twice, where 1 Samuel 6:4 has five of each; kept as printed. አናጹት 'mice' (?) is the whole form of the broken ጹት above. ወርቀ ሞጻ 'gold, fringe (?)' (house reading of ሞጻ, see unit 11). አጥፍኡ 'they destroyed' (አጥፍአ). ነፍስተ ብእሲ 'person-of a man' in the accusative construct. ሐመምክሙ 'you were sick' (2mp), with ነፍስተክሙ 'your persons' as accusative of respect: 'you were sick in your persons'. In በርእሰ አብያቲክሙ 'at the head of your houses' I am unsure of the intended sense (?). ቊልፈትክሙ: I am not sure of the word (?); it is the part of the body affected, probably 'hindquarters', fitting the biblical 'secret parts'.

sentences.t: ወገብሩ ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዝዎሙ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ፻፳ ፡ ሞጻ ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ወወሀብዋ ፡ ለጽዮን ፤
sentences.l: And-they-made as they-commanded-them the-Philistines: 120 fringe(?) of-gold, and-they-gave-it to-Zion;
sentences.i: They did as the Philistines had commanded them: they made 120 fringe-offerings (?) of gold and gave them to Zion.
sentences.n: ወገብሩ 'and they did'. ፻፳ is printed as 100 + 20 = 120 (the preceding unit's eight plus eight is only sixteen; the figure is kept as printed). ዘወርቅ 'of gold'. ወወሀብዋ 'and they gave it/her'; the suffix -ዋ is feminine singular, 'it' for the offering (?) rather than 'her', so ለጽዮን 'to Zion' is the recipient.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤልዎሙ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ እፎ ፡ ንፌንዋ ፡ ወመኑ ፡ ትብሉ ፡ ይሰዳ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገራ ።
sentences.l: And-again they-said-to-them: How may-we-send her, and who, you-say, may-he-send-her-off(?) into her-land?
sentences.i: And again they asked them, 'How should we send her, and who, do you say, is to send her off (?) to her own land?'
sentences.n: ዘከመ እፎ 'in what way'. ንፌንዋ 1cp subjunctive of ፈነወ 'send'. ትብሉ 'do you say', an inserted parenthesis. ይሰዳ 3ms subjunctive 'let him drive/send her off' (root ሰደ, uncertain to me (?)).

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ መሰግላነ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ያምጽኡ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ ናቃት ፡ እለ ፡ ተበኵራ ፡ በአሐቲ ፡ ጊዜ ፡ ወይርሐኑ ፡ ሰረገላተ ፡ ዲቤሆሙ ፡ ወይክልኡ ፡ እጐላቲሆሙ ፡ ወይዕጽዉ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤት ፡ ወይፅምድዎን ፡ ይኅድግዎን ፡ ይሖራ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ፈቀዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-them again the-diviners of-the-Philistines: Let-them-bring two she-camels(?) which have-borne-firstborn at one time, and-let-them-load(?) carts upon-them, and-let-them-shut their-young in-a-house, and-let-them-yoke them, let-them-leave them, let-them-go where they-wish;
sentences.i: The Philistine diviners said again, 'Let them bring two she-camels (?) that have both borne their first young at the same time (?), and let them harness carts to them (?); let them hold back their young and shut them in a house, yoke the animals, leave them, and let them go where they wish.
sentences.n: Allusion to 1 Samuel 6:7–9 (the cart and the nursing cows). Here the animals are ናቃት, which I take as 'she-camels' (cf. Arabic nāqa) (?), and they are called አግማል 'camels' afterward (unit 19); the biblical cows are not named in this text. ተበኵራ 'have borne firstborn' (ተበኵረ). ይርሐኑ: root unclear (?); the sense 'load/hitch' is from context. እጐላቲሆሙ 'their young'. ይዕጽዉ 'let them shut'. ይፅምድዎን 'let them yoke them' (ጸምደ 'bind, yoke'). The jussives ይኅድግዎን and ይሖራ continue the list without ወ.

sentences.t: ወለእመ ፡ አርትዓ ፡ ለኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ዮጊ ፡ ናአምር ፡ ከመ ፡ ተሣሀላ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለምድርነ ፡ ወለእመሰ ፡ አውከካ ፡ ወአንጌ ፡ ገያ ፡ ወፈቀዳ ፡ ገቢአ ፡ ድኅሬሆን ፡ ናአምር ፡ ከመ ፡ ተምዕዐነ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወኢያእተተ ፡ መቅሠፍቶ ፡ እስከ ፡ ያጠፍአነ ፡ ኪያነሂ ፡ ወሀገርነ ።
sentences.l: and-if they-go-straight to-Jerusalem, then we-shall-know that God-has-had-mercy on-our-land; but-if they-disturb(?) and አንጌ(?) ገያ(?) and-they-wished returning behind-them, we-shall-know that God-was-angry-with-us and-has-not-removed his-scourge until he-destroys us, us-too, and-our-land.
sentences.i: If they go straight to Jerusalem, then we shall know that God has had mercy on our land; but if they balk (?) and turn aside (?) and want to go back after their young, then we shall know that God is angry with us and has not withdrawn his scourge until he destroys us and our land.'
sentences.n: አርትዓ 'they went straight' (ርትዐ 'be straight'); ዮጊ 'then' (?). ተሣሀላ 'he had mercy' (ተሣሀለ with ለ- of the one pitied; -ኣ 'her' anticipates ለምድርነ). The clause አውከካ ወአንጌ ገያ is hard for me (?): አውከካ may be 3fp of a verb አውከከ 'be unsettled, balk' (?), and አንጌ ... ገያ 'turn aside' is a guess from the context; the tokens are not parsed. ፈቀዳ ገቢአ ድኅሬሆን 'they wished to return behind them (the young)'. ተምዕዐነ 'was angry with us'. ኢያእተተ 'has not removed' (አእተተ). እስከ ያጠፍአነ 'until he destroys us'. ኪያነሂ accusative 'us also'.

sentences.t: ወገብሩ ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዝዎሙ ፡ ማርያነ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ለመኳንንቲሆሙ ፡ ወአስተፉነውዋ ፡ ወገነዩ ፡ ላቲ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-did as they-commanded-them the-priests(?)-of the-Philistines to-their-governors, and-sent-her-off, and-did-homage(?) to-her;
sentences.i: The governors did as the Philistine priests (?) had told them; they sent her off and paid her homage (?).
sentences.n: አስተፉነውዋ 'they sent her off' (the causative reflexive አስተፈነወ, 'send away'). ገነዩ ላቲ: ገነየ 'bow, serve, do homage' (?), ላቲ 'to/for her'; the next verse picks it up as a test of respect (ኢገነዩ ላቲ, unit 20). ማርያነ is the construct plural 'ማርያን-of' and the subject of አዘዝዎሙ, as in unit 13 (ማርያነ ኢሎፍሊ); the same group as ማርያኒሆሙ above, not the መሰግላን 'diviners' of unit 16.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ አርትዓ ፡ እማንቱ ፡ አግማል ፡ ለፍኖተ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወበጽሐአ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐውደ ፡ እክል ፡ ወተቀበልዋ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ዘመድከ ፤
sentences.l: And-then went-straight those camels to-the-road-of the-land-of Judah, and-they-reached to the-threshing-floor-of grain, and-received-her the-house-of your-kinsman;
sentences.i: Then the camels went straight along the road to the land of Judah and reached a threshing floor, where your kinsman's household received her.
sentences.n: Here the animals are named: እማንቱ አግማል 'those camels' (see unit 16). ፍኖተ ብሔረ ይሁዳ 'road-of land-of Judah', a double construct. ወበጽሐአ 'they reached' (በጽሐ), a form with a stray ኣ ending: kept as printed. ዐውደ እክል 'circle/floor-of grain' = threshing floor (1 Samuel 6:12–14, Beth-shemesh, not named here). ቤተ ዘመድከ 'house-of your kinsman', addressed to Solomon.

sentences.t: ወእለሰ ፡ ኢተቀበልዋ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ዳን ፡ እለ ፡ ኢገነዩ ፡ ላቲ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይሬእይዋ ፡ አኅለቆሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በመዐት ፤
sentences.l: But-those who-did-not-receive-her, the-men-of the-house-of Dan, who did-not-do-homage to-her while seeing her, destroyed-them God in-wrath;
sentences.i: But the men of the house of Dan, who did not receive her or pay her homage as they looked on her, God destroyed in his wrath;
sentences.n: ወእለሰ 'but as for those' (-ሰ contrastive). ሰብአ ቤተ ዳን 'men-of house-of Dan' where I expected Beth-shemesh from 1 Samuel 6:19 (struck for looking at the Ark); the text says Dan, kept as printed. እንዘ ይሬእይዋ 'while they see her'. አኅለቆሙ 'he destroyed them' (አኅለቀ, 'bring to an end').

sentences.t: ወለእሙንቱሰ ፡ ዕፀወ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ሠፀርዎን ፡ ወለእማንቱኒ ፡ አግማል ፡ ረሰይዎን ፡ መሥዋዕተ ፡ ወገብአት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ውስተ ፡ መካና ።
sentences.l: and-as-for-them, wood-of the-cart they-split(?), and-those-camels they-made a-sacrifice; and-returned Zion into her-place.
sentences.i: They split up the wood of the cart (?) and made a sacrifice of the camels, and Zion went back to her place.
sentences.n: Echo of 1 Samuel 6:14 (the cart split for the fire and the cows offered). ወለእሙንቱሰ 'and as for them' (contrastive -ሰ). ሠፀርዎን 'they split them' (ሠፀረ, 'cut, split' (?)); ረሰይዎን 'they made them' with ረሰየ + a second object መሥዋዕተ 'sacrifice'. ገብአት 'she returned'; መካና 'her place'. The place is the Temple in Jerusalem in this telling.

sentences.t: ወአሜሃ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ሀለወት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤት ፡ ተልእካ ፡ ሳሙኤል ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወተከሥተ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ራእይ ፡ ወትንቢት ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ዘያሠምሮ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ግብሩ ፡ ወኰነኖሙ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ ፵ወ፰ ፡ ዓመተ ።
sentences.l: And-then while she-was in-the-house, ministered(?) Samuel the-prophet, and-was-revealed to-him vision and-prophecy, and-he-was one-who-pleased God in-all his-deeds, and-he-judged Israel 40 and 8 years.
sentences.i: While she was in the house, Samuel the prophet served her (?); vision and prophecy were revealed to him, and he pleased God in all his deeds and judged Israel for forty-eight years.
sentences.n: ተልእካ: I read ተልእከ 'he served/ministered' + -ኣ 'her' (?), Samuel as attendant of the Ark (1 Samuel 3–7). ተከሥተ ሎቱ 'was revealed to him' (ተከሥተ, passive). ዘያሠምሮ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'one who pleases God'. ኰነነ 'he judged' (ኰነነ, D stem), with ለእስራኤል. ፵ወ፰ ዓመተ is 40 + (ወ 'and') + 8, accusative of time ዓመተ; the sum 48 is as printed.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ሰአሉ ፡ ሕዝብነ ፡ ያንግሥ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ እለ ፡ አውዶሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him asked our-people that-would-make-king for-them God, like the-nations that surround-them;
sentences.i: After him our people asked that God make a king reign over them, like the nations around them;
sentences.n: 1 Samuel 8:5. ሕዝብነ 'our people' (ሕዝብ with -ነ). ያንግሥ 3ms subjunctive of the causative አንገሠ 'make king' (ንግሠ), 'that he set up (a king)'. እለ አውዶሙ 'who are round about them' (አውድ 'circuit').

sentences.t: ወቀብኦ ፡ ሳሙኤል ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ለሳኦል ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ፵ ፡ ዓ ፡ መተ ፤
sentences.l: And-anointed-him Samuel the-prophet, Saul the-king; and-he-also reigned 40 ዓ መተ;
sentences.i: Samuel the prophet anointed Saul as king, and he too reigned forty years;
sentences.n: 1 Samuel 10:1. ቀብኦ 'he anointed him' (ቀብአ) + ለሳኦል 'Saul' in apposition (ለ- marks the object). ነግሠ 'he reigned'. The number is ፵ ፡ ዓ ፡ መተ: ዓመተ 'years' is printed split into ዓ and መተ with word-spaces. Kept as printed.

sentences.t: ወለሊሁሰ ፡ እምሕዝበ ፡ ብንያሚ ፡ እንተ ፡ ትንእስ ፡ በትር ፡ እምሕዝበ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: and-he-himself was from-people-of Benjamin, which is small(?) of-rod from-people-of Israel;
sentences.i: and he himself was from the tribe of Benjamin, the smallest rod (tribe) among the people of Israel;
sentences.n: ለሊሁሰ 'he himself, however'. በትር 'rod, staff' is used here for 'tribe', as in Hebrew maṭṭeh/šēbeṭ; እንተ ትንእስ በትር 'which is small as to rod', i.e. 'the smallest tribe' (1 Samuel 9:21). Benjamin, the tribe of Saul.

sentences.t: ወቀብኦ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ሳሙኤል ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ለአቡከ ፡ ዳዊት ።
sentences.l: And-anointed-him again Samuel the-prophet, your-father David.
sentences.i: And Samuel the prophet anointed again your father David.
sentences.n: 1 Samuel 16:13. ካዕበ 'again, a second time' (Samuel's second anointing of a king). The comforters keep speaking to Solomon, so 'your father' is David.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ተኣኀዙ ፡ ቀትለ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሳኦል ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ተመውአ ፡ ሳኦል ፡ ወሞተ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ናታን ፡ ወልዱ ።
sentences.l: And-when took-hold(reciprocal) battle-of the-Philistines with Saul the-king, was-defeated Saul and-died with Nathan his-son.
sentences.i: When the Philistines' battle was joined with King Saul, Saul was defeated and died with his son Nathan.
sentences.n: 1 Samuel 31. ተኣኀዙ ቀትለ is 'they took hold of battle' (idiom, 'joined battle'); ተኣኀዙ has no stated subject (the armies, 3mp); ቀትለ is the construct 'battle-of' (ቀትል 'killing, battle'), taking ኢሎፍሊ: 'they took hold of the Philistines' battle with Saul'. ተመውአ 'was defeated, overcome' (ተመውአ, passive-reflexive of መውአ 'conquer'). The son is named ናታን Nathan where the Bible has Jonathan; kept as printed. ወልዱ 'his son'.

sentences.t: ወእለ ፡ ተርፉ ፡ ደቂቁ ፡ ፈቀዱ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንሥእዋ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ሶበ ፡ አእመሩ ፡ ሞተ ፡ አቡሆሙ ፡ ወእኁሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: And those who-remained, his-sons, wished to-take Zion when they-learned the-death-of their-father and-their-brother;
sentences.i: His surviving sons wanted to take Zion when they learned of the death of their father and their brother;
sentences.n: ተርፉ 'they remained' (ተረፈ). ደቂቁ 'his sons' (ደቂቅ, plural). The remnant of Saul's house (this scene is not in the biblical account as I know it; it is a Kebra Nagast development). ይንሥእዋ ለጽዮን 'take her, Zion'. ሞተ አቡሆሙ 'death-of their father'.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ፈቀዱ ፡ ኀቢኦታ ፡ ወአግዕዞታ ፡ እስከ ፡ ቈላተ ፡ ጌላቡሔ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይንሥኦሙ ፡ አቡከ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወአበየቶሙ ፡ ተነሥኦ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ አቡከ ፡ ወይነሥኣ ፡ እምሀገሮሙ ፡ ኢበመሥዋዕት ፡ ወኢበዕጣን ፡ ወአጸንሕሖ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢይትከሀል ፡ ነሢኦታ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ፈቃዳ ፡ ወፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-then when they-wished to-hide-her and-to-carry-her-off as-far-as the-valley-of Gelaboe so-that-not take-them your-father David, she-refused-them to-be-lifted until came your-father and-took-her from their-town, not by-sacrifice and-not by-incense; and-he-waited, for it-is-not-possible to-take Zion without her-will and-the-will-of God;
sentences.i: Then they wanted to hide her and carry her off as far as the valley of Gilboa so that your father David could not take her from them (?), but she refused to be lifted until your father came and took her from their town, without sacrifice or incense. He waited (?), for Zion cannot be taken except by her own will and the will of God;
sentences.n: ኀቢኦታ 'to hide her' (ኀብአ); አግዕዞታ 'to carry her away' (አግዐዘ, causative). ቈላተ ጌላቡሔ 'valley-of Gelaboe' = Gilboa, where Saul died (1 Samuel 31). ከመ ኢይንሥኦሙ is literally 'that he not take them'; 'them' would be the sons, so 'take her from them' is a guess (?). አበየቶሙ 'she refused them', ተነሥኦ 'being lifted' (?) (infinitive of ተነሥአ, Gt of ነሥአ 'take'; ተንሥአ 'rise' is the other reading). ኢበመሥዋዕት ወኢበዕጣን 'not with sacrifice nor incense' (a negated ቢ phrase, with its subject the taking) (?). አጸንሕሖ 'he waited' (?) (an unexplained final ሖ; lemma uncertain). ኢይትከሀል 'it is not possible'. The Ark has her own will in this book, hence ፈቃዳ 'her will'. 2 Samuel 6 is the model, but the sacrificial detail differs.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ አቡከ ፡ ሶበ ፡ አርትዐ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ነሥኣ ፡ እምሀገረ ፡ ሰማርያ ፡ ወአብኣ ፡ ዝየ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ እንዘ ፡ ያፅሕስ ፡ በእገሪሁ ፡ በቅድሜሃ ፡ ወይጠፍሕ ፡ በእደዊሁ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ፍሥሓሃ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተንሥአት ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትምጻእ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አቡከ ።
sentences.l: And-again, your-father, when he-set-things-right(?) and-reigned over Israel, took-her from the-city-of Samaria and-brought-her here Jerusalem while he-danced(?) with-his-feet before-her and-clapped(?) with-his-hands on-account-of her-joy, for she-rose for-him to-come (to) the-city-of David your-father.
sentences.i: Later, when your father had put things right (?) and reigned over Israel, he took her from the city of Samaria and brought her here to Jerusalem, dancing (?) before her on his feet and clapping (?) his hands for joy of her, since she had risen for him to come to the city of David your father.
sentences.n: 2 Samuel 6 (David brings the Ark up, dancing). The text says ሀገረ ሰማርያ 'city of Samaria' where the biblical place is Kiriath-jearim/Obed-edom's house; Samaria was built later, so this is the book's own wording, kept as printed. አርትዐ 'he became upright / set right' (?). ያፅሕስ 'he danced' (?) and ይጠፍሕ 'he clapped' (?): both roots are uncertain to me and I follow the biblical scene. እስመ ተንሥአት ሎቱ 'for she rose for him', i.e. she consented to go. ከመ ትምጻእ ሀገረ ዳዊት 'that she come (to) the city-of David'.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱሰ ፡ ዘትብል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘሖረት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሀገሮሙ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወፈ ፡ ቀደት ፡ ለሊሃ ፡ ኢይክል ፡ ከሊኦታ ፡ ወኢ፩ ፡ እስመ ፡ በፈቃዳ ፡ ተሐውር ፡ ወበፈቃዳ ፡ ትገብእ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ሠምረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-this which you-say concerning that-went Zion their-city to-the-land-of Ethiopia: if wished God and she-wished (ፈ ቀደት) herself, none-can hinder-her, nor (ኢ፩) one, for by-her-will she-goes and-by-her-will she-returns, if God is-pleased;
sentences.i: As for what you say about Zion having gone to their city in the land of Ethiopia: if God wished it, and she herself wished it, no one can hinder her, not even one; for she goes by her own will and returns by her own will, if God is pleased.
sentences.n: ዘትብል 'which you say' (2ms), Solomon's lament; the comforters now answer it. በእንተ ዘሖረት 'about that she went' (ሖረ). The tokens ፈ ፡ ቀደት ('she wished') and ኢ፩ are broken in the source and kept as printed: ፈ ፡ ቀደት is ፈቀደት with a stray space, and ወኢ፩ looks like ወኢአሐዱ 'and not one' with the numeral ፩ 'one' standing for the word (?). ኢይክል ከሊኦታ 'none can hinder her' (ከሀለ/ከልአ). ተሐውር, ትገብእ: 3fs imperfects 'she goes, she returns'. ለእመ ሠምረ 'if he is pleased'.

sentences.t: ወለእመሰ ፡ ኢገብአት ፡ ይኩን ፡ ሥምረቱ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወለነሰ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሀለወት ፡ ኀቤነ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ዘሐነጽከ ፡ ለነ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: and-if she-does-not-return, let-be the-good-pleasure of-God; and-as-for-us, if wished God, remains with-us Jerusalem, which you-built for-us, the-house-of God.
sentences.i: And if she does not return, let that be God's good pleasure. As for us, if God wills, Jerusalem remains with us, and the house of God that you built for us.
sentences.n: ለእመሰ ... ይኩን ሥምረቱ 'but if ... let be his good pleasure' (ሥምረት 'pleasure'; ይኩን 3ms jussive of ኮነ). ለነሰ 'but as for us'. ሀለወት ኀቤነ 'she is with us' (ሀለወ 'be present'; ኀቤ- 'with'). ዘሐነጽከ ለነ 'what you built for us' (ሐነጸ 'build'; ዘ is the neuter relative, not 'where'), ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር in apposition.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ ኢታሕዝን ፡ ልበከ ፡ ወተናዘዝ ፡ በዘ ፡ ንነግረከ ፡ ወጥበብሰ ፡ እምኀቤከ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ሠረጸት ፡ ዘወሀበከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-now do-not-sadden your-heart and-be-comforted by-what we-tell-you, for wisdom is-from-with-you, she sprouted, which gave-you God, the-God-of Israel;
sentences.i: So now do not distress your heart, but be comforted by what we tell you: wisdom itself has sprung from you, wisdom that God, the God of Israel, gave you.
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ 'and now'. ኢታሕዝን ልበከ 'do not sadden your heart' (2ms causative jussive of ሐዘነ, ልበከ its object). ተናዘዝ 'be comforted' (imperative of ተናዘዘ, also 'confess'); በዘ ንነግረከ 'by that which we tell you'. ጥበብሰ 'wisdom, however' — Solomon's gift (1 Kings 3). ሠረጸት 'she sprouted' (ሠረጸ 'sprout, shoot up'); ጥበብ is feminine, so the pronoun ይእቲ and the verb are fem. ዘወሀበከ 'which he gave you'.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ነኪር ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ከመ ፡ ማኅቶት ፡ ለፀሐይ ፡ ዘኢይበቊዕ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ብሒእ ፡ ወዕጒስታር ፡ ለመዓር ፡ ኢይበቊዕ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ነገሮሙ ፡ ለአብዳን ፡ በላዕለ ፡ ጠቢብ ፡ ኢይበቊዕ ፡ ከመ ፡ ጢስ ፡ ለዐይን ፡ ወከመ ፡ ቆዕ ፡ ለስነን ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ኢይበቊዕ ፡ በላዕለ ፡ ጠቢብ ፡ ነገረ ፡ አብዳን ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: For alien to-wisdom like a-lamp to-the-sun, which does-not-avail, and-like milk(?) and-ዕጒስታር(?) to-honey does-not-avail; likewise the-words-of fools against a-wise-man does-not-avail, like smoke to-the-eye and-like ቆዕ(?) to-teeth, likewise does-not-avail against a-wise-man the-speech-of fools.
sentences.i: For folly (?) is foreign to wisdom, as a lamp is to the sun, which is of no use; and as milk (?) and ዕጒስታር (?) are to honey, of no use: likewise the words of fools against a wise man are of no use, like smoke to the eye and ቆዕ (?) to the teeth. So the speech of fools does not avail against a wise man.
sentences.n: Proverbial close, with a parallel in Proverbs 10:26 (smoke to the eyes, something sour to the teeth). ነኪር 'foreign, alien'; ለጥበብ 'to wisdom'; I take the unstated subject as folly (?). ከመ ማኅቶት ለፀሐይ 'like a lamp to the sun'. ዘኢይበቊዕ 'which does not avail' (በቊዐ 'avail, be of use'); ኢይበቊዕ negates the likeness. ብሒእ 'milk' (?) and ዕጒስታር: I cannot identify these two words (?); I give 'milk' tentatively, and ዕጒስታር is left in Geʿez. ቆዕ is also uncertain (?), perhaps 'something sour'. ጢስ 'smoke', ዐይን 'eye', ስነን 'teeth'. ነገሮሙ ለአብዳን 'words-of them, of the fools' (resumptive ለ-). The closing ፨ run is the chapter-end mark, attached to this unit and kept as printed.
